content: What are the primary operational goals and success criteria for this Tactical Control System—such as mission types it must support, priority outcomes, and any capabilities that are most critical to achieve?

The main goal is to let operators plan, launch, monitor, and recover unmanned aircraft missions reliably across different platforms, without having to use separate systems for each one. It needs to support things like reconnaissance, surveillance, target acquisition, and other ISR-style missions, with the ability to manage the aircraft and its payloads in real time.
Success is mostly about mission effectiveness and responsiveness: operators can get the right sensor data to the right people quickly, maintain situational awareness of the vehicle and payload status, and keep control even when conditions change. The most critical capabilities are common mission planning, live vehicle and payload control, ingesting and processing sensor feeds, and sharing mission products and tasking information with the broader command-and-control environment.
